cases.evaluation_input:
# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | method | retained by cutoff
  Formulate slice selection as a bilevel problem: the inner problem selects the transport plan minimizing projected-space cost, while the outer objective evaluates that induced plan with the original-space cost.

- T001 | method | retained by cutoff
  Differentiate and optimize a Gaussian-perturbed expectation of a possibly nonsmooth slice objective using Monte Carlo Stein gradients, exposed eventually as a generic PyTorch loss for arbitrary objectives.

- T002 | method | abandoned by cutoff
  Evaluate a partial-transport SWGG variant in which the projected 1D problem selects a fixed number of matched pairs before the induced correspondence is scored in the original space.

- T003 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Make the transport cost exponent configurable and compare W1 against squared W2 objectives rather than fixing a single ground-cost power.

- T004 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Ablate the Monte Carlo budget used by the perturbation-gradient estimator, evaluating sample counts spanning 5 to 1000 draws.

- T005 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Ablate the Gaussian perturbation scale used to smooth the objectives, including values from 0.01 through 1.0.

- T006 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Experimentally characterize and optimize both the projected inner cost G and the original-space lifted-plan cost F, together with their smoothed variants, instead of evaluating only one level.

- T007 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Test perturbation-gradient optimization as input dimension increases, including high-dimensional synthetic problems up to dimension 100.

- T008 | method | retained by cutoff
  Use the unperturbed objective value as a control-variate baseline in the Stein estimator, estimating gradients from F(theta+epsilon z)-F(theta) or G(theta+epsilon z)-G(theta).

- T009 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Evaluate Gaussian filtering or local Gaussian averaging of noisy Stein-gradient estimates as an additional gradient-smoothing component.

- T010 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Evaluate the objectives on multiple synthetic distribution families—Gaussian, separated or outlier-contaminated Gaussian, and uniform distributions.

- T011 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Compare objective landscapes and optimization across empirical sample sizes, including small n=4 examples and large n=1000 examples.

- T012 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Compare optimization of the perturbed objective using plain SGD, momentum SGD, and Adam under shared synthetic data and run settings.

- T013 | method | superseded by observed T031
  Generalize the one-dimensional slice from a linear direction to a trainable single-layer Linear-ReLU neural projector and perturb all projector parameters for Stein-gradient optimization.

- T014 | method | abandoned by cutoff
  Use a generalized circular slice that orders points by polar angle around a learnable center, and optimize that center on concentric-circle data.

- T015 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Compare induced transport plans and original-space costs for exact OT, random-search linear min-SWGG, and neural DGSWP on a controlled two-dimensional eight-Gaussians-to-two-moons problem.

- T016 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Ablate neural-projector depth by comparing one-hidden-layer and two-hidden-layer projector architectures.

- T017 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate DGSWP as a gradient-flow loss by alternating inner optimization of the learned projector with outer updates of the source particles toward a fixed target.

- T018 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate gradient flows across Swiss-roll, two-moons, and Gaussian targets, including both two-dimensional and 500-dimensional Gaussian settings.

- T019 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare gradient-flow performance of DGSWP with linear and neural projectors against SWD, ASWD, random-search and optimized min-SWGG, and Max-SW baselines.

- T020 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Benchmark gradient-flow runtime scaling across dimensions 2–100 and empirical sample counts 10–1000 for the sliced and generalized-plan methods.

- T021 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Summarize repeated gradient-flow runs using median trajectories with quantile uncertainty bands.

- T022 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Evaluate DGSWP-based conditional flow matching on an eight-Gaussians source and two-moons target synthetic task.

- T023 | method | active at cutoff
  Use DGSWP-induced minibatch transport plans to pair source and target samples for conditional flow matching.

- T024 | experiment | superseded by observed T034
  Evaluate conditional-flow generation with exact Wasserstein cost between generated and target samples.

- T025 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Compare independent CFM and exact OT-CFM against DGSWP-CFM using both linear and neural DGSWP projectors.

- T026 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Ablate reuse of each precomputed DGSWP coupling map across 1, 4, 10, 40, or 100 conditional-flow minibatch updates.

- T027 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate conditional-flow checkpoints under Euler and adaptive DoPri5 ODE integration.

- T028 | method | active at cutoff
  Extend DGSWP to the Poincaré ball by ordering points with a learnable Busemann map, evaluating induced pairs with hyperbolic ground distance, and using manifold-aware updates for slice and source parameters.

- T029 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate hyperbolic gradient flows on wrapped-normal targets positioned near the center and boundary of the Poincaré ball, comparing DGSWP with SWD and HHSW.

- T030 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Compare hyperbolic gradient flow using an optimized Busemann slice against a variant labeled as using no slice optimization.

- T031 | method | retained by cutoff
  Use a trainable one-hidden-layer ReLU neural network as a nonlinear one-dimensional projector and optimize all of its parameters with the perturbation-gradient estimator.

- T032 | method | retained by cutoff
  Retain or roll back to the inner projector state with the lowest observed smoothed objective during projector optimization.

- T033 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate the Stein control-variate estimator by comparing optimization with and without subtracting the unperturbed objective, over repeated runs and both matched and stability-adjusted learning rates.

- T034 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate conditional-flow variants using mean FID over training checkpoints, with separate Euler and DoPri5 reports.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Evaluate conditional-flow image generation on CIFAR-10 using a time-conditioned UNet training setup.

  Use an invertible nonlinear MLP alignment map built from invertible linear layers and invertible LeakyReLU activations in place of a purely orthogonal rotation.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Adopt an additive-coupling RevNet as the nonlinear invertible alignment map, while retaining an orthogonal Rotation implementation as the linear baseline.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Run an IOI causal-abstraction experiment on Llama-3.2-1B by intervening at a selected transformer layer and aligned hidden subspace with Rotation or RevNet, comparing pretrained, fully randomized, random-unembedding, random-embedding, and tied random-embedding/unembedding model conditions; preprocess examples so the two candidate answers correspond to distinguishable tokenizer outputs.

- T006 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Ablate nonlinear-map capacity on the synthetic MLP tasks by sweeping RevNet internal hidden width from 1 through the full representation dimension over five fixed seeds and, during MLP training progression, comparing Rotation with RevNets using 1, 5, or 10 coupling blocks at the task representation width and a 10-block width-128 variant.

- T007 | experiment | active at cutoff

# Evaluation trajectory prefix

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Test whether CoSTEER's implementation knowledge transfers across Alpha101: build knowledge from ground-truth implementations for factors 0–63, then give the agent factors 64–95 without ground truth for ten evolution rounds and reveal ground truth only for final evaluation.

- T001 | method | superseded by observed T011
  Build factor candidates from financial PDFs by using an LLM to identify stock-selection quantitative reports, extract factor names and formulas, test daily computability from available China A-share data, and remove semantic duplicates. Bound long prompts by shrinking report text.

- T002 | method | active at cutoff
  Use CoSTEER's graph knowledge base to retrieve examples by task component and by links among errors, failed traces, feedback, and successful implementations. Prefer version 2, mix ground-truth-evaluated and ordinary knowledge, pass feedback for the exact current implementation directly, and avoid duplicating it among generic failure examples.

- T003 | method | active at cutoff
  Implement each quantitative factor with a scenario-conditioned FactorCoSTEER loop: generate code, execute it, evaluate behavior and output, retain diagnostic feedback, and retrieve relevant failed and successful implementations for the next attempt. Run up to ten rounds by default and return only implementations with positive final evaluation.

- T004 | method | active at cutoff
  Evaluate generated factor code for successful execution, single-column finite daily output, index and row-count agreement, and—when ground truth exists—either more than 99% elementwise agreement within 1e-6 or mean and rank IC above 0.99. Use the symmetric row-count ratio min(generated, truth) / max(generated, truth). During CoSTEER critique, flag future-data leakage and feed diagnostic failures into correction attempts.

- T005 | method | active at cutoff
  Establish an iterative Qlib factor-research loop that proposes factor hypotheses from the scenario and prior feedback, converts them into FactorCoSTEER tasks, tests new factors cumulatively with the SOTA library, and uses backtest feedback to decide whether to retain them. Early prompts favored progressively deeper factor types and transaction-cost-aware performance.

- T006 | method | active at cutoff
  Turn model descriptions in PDFs into structured implementation tasks containing name, formulation, architecture, variables, hyperparameters, and Tabular, TimeSeries, or Graph type. When multiple documents describe the same model, keep the entry with the most complete formulation.

- T007 | method | active at cutoff
  Implement quantitative models with ModelCoSTEER: iteratively generate and execute model.py, evaluate it under the active scenario, store successes and failures, and condition later attempts on recent failures, similar successful code, evaluator feedback, and the current workspace. Run ten iterations by default and return only positively evaluated implementations.

- T008 | method | active at cutoff
  Establish an iterative Qlib model-research loop that proposes one architecture change from the scenario, prior trials, code, and feedback; converts it into a structured Tabular or TimeSeries task; implements it with ModelCoSTEER; and compares its trained and backtested performance with the accepted model. Early search began with simple models and increased architectural complexity after successful changes.

- T009 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate generated daily stock factors by combining them with factors and Alpha158 features in a Qlib CSI300 experiment using LGBM. Train on 2008–2014, validate on 2015–2016, and test and backtest on 2017–2020 against SH000300 with a TopkDropout portfolio strategy and configured trading costs.

- T010 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Benchmark generated models on CSI300 using 20 Alpha158 features and next-period close returns. Train on 2008–2014, validate on 2015–2016, and test and backtest on 2017–2020; support tabular and 20-step time-series inputs, and report IC, rank IC, and TopkDropout portfolio metrics with trading costs.

- T011 | method | active at cutoff
  Revise PDF-derived factor construction to request structured JSON for names, formulas, and viability; retain only viable candidates; and send them directly to experiment loading. Remove the earlier embedding-and-LLM deduplication stage.

  Train views with an intra-angle objective that penalizes cosine alignment among normalized directions from the original teacher output to each augmented view, at both feature and logit levels.

  Supervise every augmented-view classifier with ground-truth cross-entropy and add the summed branch loss to training with coefficient 0.8.

  Directly integrate the augmented teacher into the DKD distiller so the student receives the ensemble through DKD while branch classification and angular losses are added to the training losses.

- T003 | method | active at cutoff
  Use constrained inter-angle losses that associate each generated feature/logit view with its source teacher output while adding a pairwise view-diversity value detached through `.item()`; the logit representation uses temperature 4 after the April update.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate five-view Angular-KD with CRD on CIFAR-100 across teacher/student architectures; the public exemplar uses ResNet32x4 to ResNet8x4 for 240 epochs with all four angular-loss weights enabled.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Use TeKAP-style Gaussian perturbations as a comparison with three noisy feature/logit views: the initial implementation pre-scales Gaussian noise by 0.1 before a 0.1 mixture, and later revisions mix standard-normal noise as 0.9 times the original plus 0.1 times noise; distill from the unperturbed teacher as well as the noisy views, and apply the comparison with CRD/DKD, MLKD, and ReviewKD variants.

- T006 | method | active at cutoff
  Generate multiple learned teacher views from one frozen teacher by feeding its pooled feature through parallel linear branches with branch-specific dropout, BatchNorm, and classifiers.

- T007 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Aggregate all augmented views with the original teacher using coefficients 0.8 for each view and 1.0 for the original, L2-normalize those coefficients, and apply softmax at the KD temperature to logits before summation.

- T008 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare Angular-KD compatibility runs using the DOT optimizer, which separates task- and KD-gradient momentum, against standard CRD or summed-loss training.

- T009 | method | active at cutoff
  Replace direct Angular-DKD with a combined Angular-KD, CRD, and DKD formulation: use CRD as the distiller, retain CRD feature loss, and conditionally add warm-started DKD against the augmented teacher output with coefficient 0.3.

- T010 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Test Angular-KD as a plug-in to MLKD on CIFAR-100 using weak/strong image views, augmented-teacher outputs at temperatures 1 through 6, MLKD losses, and CRD feature loss across several architecture pairs.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Test Angular-KD as a plug-in to ReviewKD on CIFAR-100 by adding augmented-teacher angular and branch losses plus output-level KD to ReviewKD's hierarchical feature loss, with model-pair-specific feature adapters.

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | method | retained by cutoff
  Train views with an intra-angle objective that penalizes cosine alignment among normalized directions from the original teacher output to each augmented view, at both feature and logit levels.

- T001 | method | retained by cutoff
  Supervise every augmented-view classifier with ground-truth cross-entropy and add the summed branch loss to training with coefficient 0.8.

- T002 | method | superseded by observed T009
  Directly integrate the augmented teacher into the DKD distiller so the student receives the ensemble through DKD while branch classification and angular losses are added to the training losses.

- T003 | method | superseded by observed T012
  Use constrained inter-angle losses that associate each generated feature/logit view with its source teacher output while adding a pairwise view-diversity value detached through `.item()`; the logit representation uses temperature 4 after the April update.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate five-view Angular-KD with CRD on CIFAR-100 across teacher/student architectures; the public exemplar uses ResNet32x4 to ResNet8x4 for 240 epochs with all four angular-loss weights enabled.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Use TeKAP-style Gaussian perturbations as a comparison with three noisy feature/logit views: the initial implementation pre-scales Gaussian noise by 0.1 before a 0.1 mixture, and later revisions mix standard-normal noise as 0.9 times the original plus 0.1 times noise; distill from the unperturbed teacher as well as the noisy views, and apply the comparison with CRD/DKD, MLKD, and ReviewKD variants.

- T006 | method | active at cutoff
  Generate multiple learned teacher views from one frozen teacher by feeding its pooled feature through parallel linear branches with branch-specific dropout, BatchNorm, and classifiers.

- T007 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Aggregate all augmented views with the original teacher using coefficients 0.8 for each view and 1.0 for the original, L2-normalize those coefficients, and apply softmax at the KD temperature to logits before summation.

- T008 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare Angular-KD compatibility runs using the DOT optimizer, which separates task- and KD-gradient momentum, against standard CRD or summed-loss training.

- T009 | method | active at cutoff
  Replace direct Angular-DKD with a combined Angular-KD, CRD, and DKD formulation: use CRD as the distiller, retain CRD feature loss, and conditionally add warm-started DKD against the augmented teacher output with coefficient 0.3.

- T010 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Test Angular-KD as a plug-in to MLKD on CIFAR-100 using weak/strong image views, augmented-teacher outputs at temperatures 1 through 6, MLKD losses, and CRD feature loss across several architecture pairs.

- T011 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Test Angular-KD as a plug-in to ReviewKD on CIFAR-100 by adding augmented-teacher angular and branch losses plus output-level KD to ReviewKD's hierarchical feature loss, with model-pair-specific feature adapters.

- T012 | method | retained by cutoff
  Use a differentiable constrained inter-angle objective by retaining the pairwise diversity term as a tensor rather than converting it with `.item()`; use the configured KD temperature for logit angular losses and a 0.2 logit margin.

- T013 | method | active at cutoff
  For Angular-KD runs using the standard CRD trainer, add temperature-scaled KL distillation from the student's logits to the augmented teacher ensemble alongside CRD feature transfer, whether or not the optional DKD term is enabled.

- T014 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate Angular-KD on ImageNet with a ResNet34 teacher and ResNet18 student for 110 epochs, batch size 512, five augmented views, and KD temperature 1.

- T015 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  On the ImageNet Angular-KD run, ablate feature-level angular objectives by setting both feature weights to zero while retaining both logit inter- and intra-angle objectives at weight 1.

- T016 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Compare end-to-end Angular-KD training with an optional two-stage protocol that first pretrains the augmented teacher/view generator for 30 CIFAR-100 epochs and then initializes distillation from the saved teacher-side checkpoint.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Aggregate the original teacher and augmented views using coefficients 1.0 and 0.8 respectively, but L1-normalize the coefficients so the weighted ensemble is a normalized sum; retain temperature-scaled softmax for logits.

cases.evaluation_input:
# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate design-matrix preconditioning for Langevin and Hamiltonian posterior samplers, using the inverse of X-transpose-X plus lambda_reg times the identity and configuring lambda_reg=1.0.

- T001 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate the samplers on a synthetic logistic contextual bandit with d=20, 50 arms, horizon 10,000, and Bernoulli rewards generated through a sigmoid link.

- T002 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Use a synthetic linear contextual-bandit benchmark with d=20, five arms, four-dimensional raw contexts, horizon 10,000, and reward standard deviation 0.5.

- T003 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  For the linear benchmark, reuse one generated context/parameter instance per seed across algorithms, repeat over configurable seeds (executed with ten), and report mean and standard deviation of cumulative regret plus the average cumulative-regret value over the final 500 steps.

- T004 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Include an SVRG-driven MALA Thompson-sampling method using minibatches and periodically refreshed reference/full gradients.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate LMC, FG-LMC, and FG-MALA on the Yahoo R6 logged-bandit data using replay-style accepted events and click-through rate, with configurations limiting the experiment to 500,000 events.

- T006 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Add a hard Feel-Good optimism term to posterior-training objectives by subtracting a weighted, capped maximum predicted reward, using the form -lambda times the sum of min(g-star, b).

- T007 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Provide a smoothed Feel-Good objective that replaces the hard cap with b - softplus(s(b-g-star))/s, with smoothing scale configurable and defaulted to 10.

- T008 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Run a sampler-and-baseline showdown spanning LMC, MALA, HMC, SVRG-LMC, later ULMC, their applicable Feel-Good/smoothed/preconditioned variants, exact linear TS, UCB/epsilon-greedy baselines, and neural TS/UCB-style baselines.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Add underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo as a Thompson-sampling posterior approximation, maintaining momentum with friction gamma and step size h.

- T005 | method | active at cutoff
  Combine trend, mean-reversion, momentum, volatility, and statistical-arbitrage technical indicators through confidence-weighted component signals.

- T006 | method | active at cutoff
  Limit ticker exposure with fixed portfolio-relative position caps, first 20 percent and then 25 percent.

- T007 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Support benchmark runs with selectable LLMs and configurable inference temperature. - T008 | method | active at cutoff
  Use a configurable multi-agent, per-ticker workflow in which selected analyst branches produce signals that are aggregated by downstream portfolio management with integrated risk control.   Frame DeepFund around the research question of whether LLMs can perform professional fund investment when evaluated in a nearly live trading arena rather than only as a trading demonstration.

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Train a continuous variance-preserving SDE sampler with an equilibrium-scaled reverse-KL trajectory objective.

- T001 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate the loss variants on multimodal synthetic energies and particle systems, including Gaussian and Student-t mixtures, Rastrigin, many-well, Lennard-Jones, and pairwise double-well targets.

- T002 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Train the continuous sampler with a stopped-dynamics log-variance objective and test multiple parameter updates from each sampled trajectory.

- T003 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate learning only the Gaussian reference, all non-schedule process parameters, or the complete process including bridge diffusion schedules.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Assess samplers with free energy, log-partition and effective-sample-size estimates plus target-appropriate Sinkhorn, MMD, mode-coverage, energy, and particle-distance diagnostics across replicated runs.

- T005 | method | retained by cutoff
  Introduce a discrete diffusion bridge initialized from a Gaussian reference, with cosine-varying diffusion and learned reverse transitions conditioned on the reference-to-target interpolation.

- T006 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Optimize the bridge with a pathwise reverse-KL loss over forward and reverse transition densities, the reference density, and terminal energy.

- T007 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare bridge rKL with pathwise gradients, bridge rKL with log-derivative gradients, and stopped-dynamics log variance for CMCD and DBS under learned and frozen process parameters.

- T008 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate on Bayesian inference targets including logistic regressions, hierarchical Seeds, Neal's Funnel, Brownian motion, Lorenz bridge, and log-Gaussian Cox processes.

- T009 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Evaluate on-policy training against temperature-annealed off-policy bridge proposals, including Gaussian/Laplace mixtures and alternatives that perturb only noise or both noise and drift.

- T010 | method | retained by cutoff
  Add log-derivative reverse-KL estimators that stop trajectory gradients and optimize centered trajectory costs through path-likelihood score terms.

- T011 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Compare constant, linear, cosine, per-step learned, and state- or time-conditioned neural bridge diffusion schedules.

- T012 | method | retained by cutoff
  Importance-weight off-policy rKL-LD with the ratio between on-policy and actual proposal densities, including the initial prior ratio and optional weight clipping or tempering.

- T013 | method | active at cutoff
  Compare a plain feed-forward bridge score with an interpolation-gradient-aware PISGradNet.

- T014 | method | active at cutoff
  Add forward- and reverse-oriented subtrajectory objectives using cumulative path-density ratios and centered per-transition rewards.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Add forward-KL bridge objectives in log-derivative and on-policy reparameterized forms using self-normalized trajectory weights.

cases.evaluation_input:
# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Use PCA to identify low-dimensional hidden-state trajectories and relate their geometry to the RNN's predicted outputs.

- T001 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Train a bias-free single-layer ReLU RNN, driven by Gaussian noise, to reproduce HMM observation sequences with categorical outputs and Sinkhorn-divergence loss.

- T002 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Ablate RNN hidden width and stochastic-input dimension across the HMM configurations.

- T003 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate HMM-RNN agreement with sequence distance, output frequencies, transition matrices, and Euclidean geometry, tuning Sinkhorn blur and aggregating multiple random seeds.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Vary HMM topology from linear chains to fully connected and cyclic systems with two to five latent states, retaining one representative configuration per topology after cleanup.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Ablate HMM persistence, emission ambiguity, and output-alphabet structure; remove the deterministic custom-emission and five-output branches from the suite.

- T006 | experiment | abandoned by cutoff
  Explore autonomous fixed points, global PCA flow fields, weight-matrix singular directions, and local Jacobian maps, then drop these broad analysis pipelines.

- T007 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Decompose local RNN updates into stochastic-input, post-ReLU input, recurrence-only, and full components, comparing their dimensionality and directional alignment along trajectories.

- T008 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Track dynamics across training checkpoints and replace a broad perturbation inventory with a focused analysis of second-order noise effects, transition rate, complex or unstable modes, and a detected bifurcation epoch.

- T009 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Ablate the magnitude of Gaussian driving noise in both behavioral and mechanistic analyses.

- T010 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Locate output-transition regions globally and within output-pair-specific latent subspaces, measuring residence time, logit-gradient changes, and local instability before switches.

- T011 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Identify direction-specific candidate kick-neuron groups and their noise-integrating populations, then causally intervene on those groups and matched controls while tracking trajectory and eigenmode changes.

- T012 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare recurrence-only and noise-driven trajectories and density contours across HMM topologies, network sizes, and noise levels.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Measure how output readout axes project into the learned low-dimensional latent plane across HMM configurations.

# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Relate prefix-conditioned loss on known training examples to their original training positions across Pythia checkpoints, scales, deduplication variants, and fine-tuned derivatives.

- T001 | method | active at cutoff
  Strengthen order detection by subtracting reference-model loss, testing the hypothesis that references sharing more training data remove more content-related variation.

- T002 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Measure how many evaluated or generated samples each direct and observational provenance test needs before its correlation or null-relative statistic becomes reliable.

- T003 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Use controlled TinyStories models to ablate batch size, epoch count, and whether the example order is fixed or reshuffled across epochs.

- T004 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Test whether provenance survives distillation, replacing KL training with cross-entropy on teacher probabilities and comparing soft teacher targets with hard argmax labels.

- T005 | method | active at cutoff
  Develop an observational n-gram test that backs off to the longest matching continuation in indexed pretraining data, then evaluates match-step statistics on generated Pythia text against shuffled nulls.

- T006 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Train a new model on teacher-generated stories and test whether its losses retain the teacher's original training-order signal.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Partition a known ordered TinyStories suffix and train comparison models from a common partial checkpoint, then correlate their likelihoods on target-generated text with partition order.

cases.evaluation_input:
# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | method | active at cutoff
  Probe image memory through masked-object identity: identify visible objects with a multimodal image analyzer and GroundingDINO/SAM2, black out an object's bounding region, generate context-plausible distractors from the original-plus-masked image with a multimodal generator (.

- T001 | method | active at cutoff
  Probe object-level color memory by estimating a boxed object's primary color with a multimodal model, pairing it with three distractors, converting the image to grayscale while retaining a red localization box, and asking the target LVLM to recover the original color. Implementations evolved from Qwen and a fixed vocabulary, expanded to include clear, gray, tan, and black-and-white, to a configurable API extractor that rejects multicolored objects.

- T002 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate the probes across three target LVLM implementations: LLaVA-v1.5-7B, MiniGPT-4, and LLaMA-Adapter-v2.

- T003 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Evaluate on the labeled img_Flickr and img_dalle image partitions.

- T004 | ablation | active at cutoff
  Evaluate option-order and query-repetition sensitivity by comparing ordered-choice queries, where the correct answer is placed successively in A/B/C/D, with repeated random-choice queries whose four options are reshuffled; recorded randomized runs use 4, 6, or 8 repetitions.

- T005 | method | retained by cutoff
  Use probe-answer accuracy averaged at image level as the membership score and evaluate separation of labels with ROC AUC.

- T006 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate the semantic probe components by reporting object-identity scores, object-color scores, and a combined object-plus-color score separately.

- T007 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate two invalid-response policies: retain all available probe accuracies or exclude probe entries whose invalid-response counter is nonzero before image-level scoring.

- T008 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate prompt wording and answer-format constraints for the memory probes, including alternative object/object-color templates and five whole-image color-recall formulations.

- T009 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Sweep target-generation temperature over 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 while holding top-p at 0.9 in the object/color probing experiments.

- T010 | method | active at cutoff
  Add a whole-image color-memory probe: use Qwen to extract distinct visible colors from the original image over three queries, remove white, black, and gray, pair each color with three other color choices, convert the image to three-channel grayscale, and ask which color was present in the original.

- T011 | method | active at cutoff
  Add a patch-reordering caption probe: split each image into a 3×3 grid, apply random non-identity permutations, generate one Qwen caption for the original and three caption distractors for each reordered version, and ask the target LVLM to select the original description using A/B/C/D options.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Calibrate candidate object and color probes against prior knowledge: reject masked-object questions whose ground-truth object is judged “Very Certain” from the visible context, reject object-color questions whose color is “Very Certain” from the object name, test distractors for plausibility, and regenerate implausible distractors.

# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Use A5 state tracking as the initial length-generalization benchmark, with seeded splits, auxiliary short sequences, and masks that exclude padding from supervision.

- T001 | method | active at cutoff
  Start from a dense affine LinearCDE, wrapped in residual sequence blocks, whose input-conditioned matrix and additive term update the hidden state at every token.

- T002 | method | retained by cutoff
  Test a sparse LinearCDE by fixing a random binary mask over transition weights and applying the same mask to their gradients.

- T003 | method | active at cutoff
  Develop a diagonal transition variant and then mix its state update with a normalized Walsh-Hadamard transform, bounding learned transition factors before they act on the state.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Broaden the comparison set from Mamba and LSTM to Transformer, DeltaNet variants, GatedDeltaNet, DeltaProduct, and RWKV6/7; an xLSTM implementation was tried but removed.

- T005 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate residual-block design across LinearCDE and Mamba baselines, settling on normalized residual blocks with an optional GLU residual.

- T006 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Expand evaluation from A5 to a seeded suite of formal-language tasks, training on short lengths and validating on longer ones with task-specific prediction masks and deterministic data generation.

- T007 | ablation | abandoned by cutoff
  Sweep LinearCDE depth on A5 with validation-based early stopping.

- T008 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Explore Snake8 and Connect Four as additional state-tracking benchmarks.

- T009 | method | active at cutoff
  Replace sequence-length-normalized controls with a fixed-step formulation that concatenates a unit time channel and scales every control channel by a configurable step size.

- T010 | method | active at cutoff
  Introduce input-conditioned block-diagonal transitions with configurable block size, allowing interaction within small state blocks without paying for a dense matrix.

- T011 | method | active at cutoff
  Experiment with smooth clipping of the transition update—first before adding the input term and later after combining both contributions—to control numerical instability.

Predict the next research decision. Return the required JSON only.

target.decision: Repeat each tracked configuration across five offset random seeds and store run-specific outputs for statistical comparison.

# Evaluation trajectory prefix

All decisions introduced before the held-out decision are shown in timezone-aware first-date order. Outcomes that were not established by the cutoff are withheld.

Observed decisions:

- T000 | method | active at cutoff
  Extend mean-only solves to predictive uncertainty by jointly solving target and sampling right-hand sides, using noisy random-feature priors and pathwise posterior correction to estimate variance and likelihood.

- T001 | method | retained by cutoff
  Represent GP and kernel-ridge inference as regularized matrix-free kernel linear systems with row and block access, multiple covariance families, and optional distributed operators.

- T002 | method | active at cutoff
  Develop accelerated sketch-and-project from small synthetic tests into a distributed solver with adaptive Nyström preconditioning and block updates, replacing several preliminary scaling configurations.

- T003 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Evaluate solver iterates by held-out posterior-mean RMSE and R-squared, adding training metrics only when a full-kernel residual pass is affordable.

- T004 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Compare SAP, preconditioned conjugate gradients, and stochastic dual descent across standard regression data, a 334-million-row taxi sample, and molecular Dockstring targets.

- T005 | method | active at cutoff
  Approximate RBF and Matérn kernels with random Fourier features and validate their convergence across feature counts before using them for posterior sampling.

- T006 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Replace preliminary exact-GP tuning experiments with a scalable procedure that fits exact GPs on repeated nearest-neighbor subsamples and averages their signal, lengthscale, and noise estimates.

- T007 | experiment | retained by cutoff
  Allow large problems to disable full-kernel residuals and instead run every right-hand side to a fixed data-pass budget.

- T008 | ablation | retained by cutoff
  Ablate SAP's Nyström preconditioner and the stochastic-dual-descent step size; an additional PCG precision comparison was attempted but dropped.

- T009 | method | abandoned by cutoff
  Explore a random-feature approximation to the Tanimoto kernel.

- T010 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Use pathwise GP posterior draws as Thompson-sampling acquisitions, optimize each draw with global proposals followed by local gradient refinement, and compare SAP, PCG, and SDD against random search.

  Evaluate paired identity recovery in both directions against no-translation, assignment, Sinkhorn, EMD, and Gromov-Wasserstein baselines using top-k accuracy and rank statistics.

  Use residual SiLU input and output adapters for each embedding space, with batch normalization and Kaiming initialization in the configuration.

- T005 | experiment | active at cutoff
  Use disjoint seeded train and validation populations, a fixed post-warmup learning rate, and early stopping on validation identity-retrieval rank.

  Test cycle-margin loss, end-to-end cycle gradients, discriminator gradient penalties, and input noise.

- T008 | method | retained by cutoff
  Optionally adversarially match within-batch cosine-similarity matrices in addition to individual embeddings.
